title: Pulse Lattice: response-time contrastboard by servepath, model family, and IO-mode
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create a new observability surface (Pulse Lattice contrastboard) that visualizes response-time distributions (p50/p95/p99) split by model family and API route, with an explicit breakdown for streaming vs synchronous (non-streaming) IO modes. The board should help SREs and runtime engineers quickly detect regressions that disproportionately affect streaming or blocking paths, reveal model-specific tail behavior, and correlate bursts to recent rollouts or infra changes. This work includes instrumentation additions (trace hook tags, new aggregation keys), metrics pipeline changes, dashboard panels, and an alerting proposal for cross-IO-mode regressions.
background: We already have several latency dashboards and cohort explorers, but investigating cross-IO-mode regressions is still manual: we join traces, run ad-hoc queries, and stitch charts. Streaming responses can exhibit different shapes (first-byte, mid-stream stalls, finalization) vs blocking calls. Recent incidents showed a model rollout that only impacted streaming tail latency for a subset of routes, which was hard to triage. The Pulse Lattice is intended to reduce MTTI (mean time to investigate) for those cases.
goals: 1) Instrumentation: add a standardized tag on traces and metrics for IO_MODE with values 'stream' or 'sync'. 2) Metrics: emit per-request latency histograms labeled by model_family, route, and IO_MODE; ensure p50/p95/p99 aggregations available in metrics store. 3) Dashboard: implement contrastboard panels that show p50/p95/p99 heatmap and time-series for stream vs sync per model-route pair, and a percentile-delta view (stream minus sync). 4) Alerts: propose a composite alert that triggers when p95 for stream > baseline by X% for a sustained window across >=2 routes.
acceptance_criteria:
- New trace tag 'io_mode' present in service traces for all ingress and runtime handlers.
- Per-request latency histogram (ms) emitted with labels: model_family, route, io_mode for 100% of production traffic.
- Dashboard deployed in Observability console with: heatmap panel (p50/p95/p99), paired time-series panels for stream vs sync, and delta panel.
- Example dashboard links included and sample queries documented.
- Alerting rule PR created with thresholds and runbook references.
- Load on metrics backend measured and within budget (no more than 12% additional cardinality cost).
implementation_notes: Instrumentation: add io_mode detection in ingress (api gateway layer) and propagate as span attribute; add same label to metrics emission path. Metrics pipeline: ensure histogram buckets match existing latency naming conventions; use aggregation micro-batching to avoid cardinality explosion. Dashboard: reuse existing chart components but add a delta calculation widget. Queries: provide both metrics-store native queries and a backup pre-aggregated-timeseries in TSDB for cheap lookups. Rollout plan: canary on 10% traffic, then 50%, then 100%.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: cardinality explosion from adding model_family x route x io_mode labels. Mitigation: collapse rare model variants into 'other' and cap route granularity to canonical route names; sample debug traces. Risk: streaming latency semantics differ (first-byte vs end-to-end). Mitigation: include separate metrics for first-byte latency and end-to-end completion latency for streaming flows.
tasks: Add io_mode span attribute in api-ingress and runtime proxies
Emit per-request histogram with model_family, route, io_mode labels
Update metrics ingestion pipeline to accept new labels and create pXX rollups
Build dashboard panels and percentile-delta widget
